title: Cancellation Policy Schedule for Stays (Guest Reservations) — Refund Windows Before Check-In
content:
# Cancellation Policy Schedule — refund windows before check-in

Every reservation in the Stays (Guest Reservations) category is booked under one of eight cancellation policies: Flexible, Moderate, Limited, Firm, Strict, Super Strict 30 Days, Super Strict 60 Days and Long-Term. This schedule sets, for each policy, the windows that decide how much of a standard-rate stay a guest cancellation dated before check-in returns.

## Schedule

| Cancellation policy | Full-refund cutoff (calendar days before check-in) | Booking grace period (elapsed hours after booking) | Grace period minimum lead (calendar days before check-in) | Partial-window cutoff (calendar days before check-in) | Partial refund | Nights forfeited in the partial window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flexible | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100.00% | 1 |
| Moderate | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 50.00% | 1 |
| Limited | 14 | 0 | 0 | 7 | 50.00% | 0 |
| Firm | 30 | 48 | 14 | 7 | 50.00% | 0 |
| Strict | 0 | 48 | 14 | 7 | 50.00% | 0 |
| Super Strict 30 Days | 0 | 0 | 0 | 30 | 50.00% | 0 |
| Super Strict 60 Days | 0 | 0 | 0 | 60 | 50.00% | 0 |
| Long-Term | 0 | 48 | 28 | 0 | 100.00% | 30 |

## What each column means

- **Full-refund cutoff** — the number of calendar days before the check-in date at or beyond which a guest cancellation refunds every nightly-based component in full. A cutoff of 0 means the policy has no full-refund window.
- **Booking grace period** — the elapsed hours after the stay was booked within which a guest cancellation refunds in full, provided the grace period minimum lead is also met. A value of 0 means the policy has no booking grace period.
- **Grace period minimum lead** — the minimum number of calendar days between the cancellation date and the check-in date for the booking grace period to apply; 0 where the policy has no grace period.
- **Partial-window cutoff** — the number of calendar days before check-in at or beyond which the partial-refund window applies once the full-refund window is missed. A cutoff of 0 means the partial window runs right up to the check-in date.
- **Partial refund** — the percent of the nightly-based components refunded in the partial-refund window, applied to the nights left after the forfeited nights.
- **Nights forfeited in the partial window** — the nights, taken from the start of the stay, that are never refunded in the partial-refund window.

## Reading the schedule

- Strict, Super Strict 30 Days, Super Strict 60 Days and Long-Term have a full-refund cutoff of 0, so none of them has a full-refund window.
- Only Firm, Strict and Long-Term have a booking grace period (48 elapsed hours); Firm and Strict require at least 14 calendar days of lead, Long-Term at least 28.
- Flexible, Moderate and Long-Term have a partial-window cutoff of 0, so their partial window runs right up to the check-in date.

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical dates)

Take a hypothetical Moderate stay whose check-in date is day D.

| Cancellation dated | Calendar days before check-in | Full-refund window (cutoff 5) | Partial window (cutoff 0) |
|---|---|---|---|
| D minus 6 | 6 | met | — |
| D minus 5 | 5 | met (at the cutoff) | — |
| D minus 4 | 4 | missed | applies: the first 1 night is forfeited and 50.00% of the remaining nights' price is refunded |

The same reading on a hypothetical Super Strict 60 Days stay: a cancellation dated exactly 60 calendar days before check-in is at the partial-window cutoff and the partial window applies; one dated 59 days before is not.
